5. THE HEATHROW THEORY

The official prosecution theory says the bomb suitcase originated in Malta, traveled through Frankfurt and was transferred onto Flight 103 at Heathrow.

But an alternative theory argues that the bomb was actually inserted at Heathrow itself.

Questions surrounding airport security and unexplained baggage have fueled this theory for decades.

If the bomb entered at Heathrow, a major component of the Malta/Libya prosecution narrative would have to be reconsidered.

6. THE LIBYA FRAME-UP / COVER-UP THEORY

This is the umbrella theory connecting everything.
It argues that investigators originally followed evidence toward Iran/PFLP-GC, but geopolitical circumstances eventually made blaming Libya far more convenient.

Critics of the conviction have alleged that evidence was suppressed, witnesses were unreliable and intelligence information was withheld.

Even mainstream reporting acknowledges that Dr. Jim Swire — whose daughter died aboard Flight 103 — became convinced that Megrahi had been wrongly convicted and that responsibility had been redirected from Iran/Syria toward Libya.

And now consider the timing:

1988: Pan Am 103 destroyed.
July 30, 2026: Netflix releases a major six-part Lockerbie series, introducing the case to an entirely new generation. (netflix.com)
August 21: Evidence previously unknown to BOTH sides reportedly emerges.
August 22: Prosecutors disclose it to the defense.
August 24: The judge postpones the long-awaited trial just before jury selection. (apnews.com)

And families themselves are saying the discovery demonstrates that information is still out there nearly four decades later. (apnews.com)

Is Lockerbie simply experiencing renewed attention because of an upcoming trial and Netflix series — or are we being prepared for another layer of the story to finally become public?

But 38 years after Lockerbie, one thing has suddenly become undeniable:

The historical record apparently wasn’t finished.
